entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Milorad Pavić was a Serbian writer, university professor, translator, literary historian and academic. He published a number of poems, short stories and novels during his lifetime, the most famous of which was the Dictionary of the Khazars (1984). Upon its release, it was hailed as "the first novel of the 21st century." Pavić's works have been translated into more than thirty languages. He was vastly popular in Europe and in South America, and was deemed "one of the most intriguing writers from the beginning of the 21st century." He won numerous prizes in Serbia and in the former Yugoslavia, and was mentioned several times as a potential candidate for the Nobel Prize in Literature.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Milorad Pavić's Dictionary of the Khazars was widely acclaimed and translated into over thirty languages, making it a significant cultural export from the former Yugoslavia. Its influence can be seen in subsequent literary works that explored postmodern and postcolonial themes.
